applicant_utility.summary: There is nothing extra to submit for the Wien Scholarship - it rides on your Brandeis application, so the real work is the Common Application plus a strong CSS Profile filed by your plan's deadline (Nov. 2 for EDI/EA, Jan. 15 for EDII/RD). Because the award equals your full demonstrated financial need, the quality and completeness of your financial documentation directly determines the size of the cheque. Build the file around both strong academics and sustained community involvement, since Brandeis explicitly weighs extracurricular and community contribution.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International applicants with genuine financial need, strong academics, and a sustained record of community involvement who want need-based funding without a separate scholarship application.
application_readiness_checklist: File the Common App or Coalition Application by your plan deadline (Nov. 2 EDI/EA; Jan. 15 EDII/RD)
Complete the CSS Profile by the same date as your admission application - financial aid deadlines match admission deadlines
Assemble complete income and asset documentation early; the award equals need established after a full review
Document community involvement with roles, hours, and impact, not just membership lists
Plan to reapply for financial aid each academic year and maintain satisfactory academic progress
common_rejection_risks: Filing the CSS Profile late or not at all - need-based consideration depends on complete financial documentation
Overstating or omitting family finances; Brandeis verifies credentials and falsified materials can cost the offer
Thin extracurricular or community evidence despite strong grades
Assuming a separate scholarship essay exists and leaving the admission application itself under-polished
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Because the award is set at full demonstrated financial need, any gap depends on your family's determined contribution; costs beyond demonstrated need, such as personal travel, are not addressed by the award.
document_audit: The CSS Profile is required for institutional need-based aid - skipping it leaves the Wien award undeterminable
Documents must come directly from schools and officials; Brandeis verifies credentials and may withdraw offers for falsified materials
No separate scholarship application exists, so nothing extra will rescue a weak admission file
alerts: Financial aid deadlines match admission-plan deadlines - missing the CSS Profile date weakens both aid and Wien consideration
Renewal requires annual reapplication; need is re-established each academic year
Lookalike awards exist (Watanabe Scholarship for students from Japan, Davis UWC Scholars) with different eligibility - only Wien is the general international need-based award
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Common/Coalition Application + CSS Profile by your admission-plan deadline -> automatic Wien review inside the admission decision -> award notice included with the admission decision -> annual financial aid reapplication for renewal.
